subject: Reconciling committed revenue: outstanding discount approvals for Blue Ridge
content:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Reconciling committed revenue: outstanding discount approvals for Blue Ridge

Team — quick one before EOD. Blue Ridge (deal DEAL-8473) is sitting in the forecast as a partial commit for Q4 with a $1.1M ACV. Procurement pushed a 25% discount in the SOW and Sales marked it as "Committed - Legal/Proc". Finance flagged the discount as outside our standard cap and wants Deal Desk sign-off before we count the full amount.

Ask: can Deal Desk confirm whether the 25% is approvable under the current quota/discount playbook? If not, we need to either: 1) update the forecast to reflect conservative ARR, or 2) escalate for one-off approval.

Attached: pricing-redline-dealdesk.xlsx (redlines from Sales). Also attaching the latest SOW we received (BLR-SOW-v2.pdf).

Quick bullets:
- ACV on opp: $1,100,000
- Requested discount: 25% (applied to subscription + first-year services)
- Committed stage: Sales marked as Committed (forecast category: commit)
- Requested by: Sam Peters, Blue Ridge (procurement contact)

No need to loop legal yet — primary gating is pricing thresholds and finance recognition. Can someone from Deal Desk/FPS confirm next steps?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---

From: Sam Peters <s.peters@blueridge.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@blueridge.ai
Date: 2026-09-01T12:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reconciling committed revenue: outstanding discount approvals for Blue Ridge

Jordan — thanks for the note. We appreciate how fast your team has moved. A couple clarifications from our side: we are requesting 25% off list because we are consolidating three Redwood-powered products across supply chain and forecasting; the initial SOW includes a 12-month onboarding block and a volume commitment.

We can sign immediately if the discount is approved by your team. Please let us know the official path for approval and any additional documentation you require. I included procurement for invoicing timelines.

Regards,
Sam Peters
Head of Procurement
Blue Ridge Logistics

Attachment: BLR-SOW-v2.pdf (SOW, redlined by BLR)

---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Peters <s.peters@blueridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reconciling committed revenue: outstanding discount approvals for Blue Ridge

Sam — great, appreciate the clarity. Quick proposal to keep the deal moving without overstating our forecast:

Proposed mutual action plan:
- Sales to secure signature on the SOW with a clear clause that the 25% discount is "subject to final Deal Desk approval" (we'll add this language).
- Deal Desk (Marissa) to review the redline workbook and indicate whether the discount is within an approvable exception band or requires escalated approval.
- If Deal Desk cannot approve, Finance (Laura) and Sales will reconcile the committed amount in the forecast — we should surface the deal as "Commit (pending final pricing approval)" in the forecast instead of counting full ACV.
- Target: decision within 48 hours to avoid slipping booking to next quarter.

I've attached the redline workbook you requested (pricing-redline-dealdesk.xlsx) and added a column that shows the effective ARR under the 25% discount vs our standard cap.

Jordan

Attachment: pricing-redline-dealdesk.xlsx (sales redlines + effective ARR calc)

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sam Peters <s.peters@blueridge.ai>
Date: 2026-09-02T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reconciling committed revenue: outstanding discount approvals for Blue Ridge

Jordan — taking point. Quick read of the workbook: the blended discount (services + subscription) pushes the effective unit economics below our permitted threshold for standard discounting. Per the deal desk playbook: discounts >20% require VP-level approval and must be reserved for strategic expansion accounts with clear ROI milestones.

Options:
1) Approve a capped discount at 20% under Deal Desk authority and request that Sales negotiate the incremental 5% as a usage milestone (e.g., 10% of the overage becomes active after hitting X throughput). This keeps the recognized ACV at a conservative level.
2) Escalate for one-off 25% approval to Finance/Revenue ops (requires justification memo and a forecast impact note).

If we choose #1, I can greenlight today and update the HubSpot record (hubspot:2345789) and instruct forecasting to count the deal at the 20% effective ACV. If Sales wants #2, please provide a short memo (1 paragraph) on strategic rationale.

Also: please do not move the opportunity to firm "Commit" in the forecast until we have Deal Desk sign-off or an explicit CFO-level exception. Marking it as "Commit (pending pricing)" in the forecast keeps us compliant with revenue recognition policy.

Marissa Cole
Head of Deal Desk Operations
Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sam Peters <s.peters@blueridge.ai>
Date: 2026-09-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reconciling committed revenue: outstanding discount approvals for Blue Ridge

Thanks everyone — quick decision from finance side: we can approve up to a 20% upfront discount under Deal Desk authority; anything beyond requires a one-off CFO exception and a short memo tying the incremental discount to expansion ARR and operational KPIs. Laura (cc'd) will need the revenue recognition note if Sales wants the full 25% counted as committed.

My recommendation: accept Marissa's #1, approve 20% now to get the contract signed, and treat the extra 5% as a contingent rebate tied to throughput milestones. Jordan — can you confirm that Sales will add the conditional clause to the SOW and push signature? Sam — if you can accept the 20% with the milestone structure, we'll fast-track the paperwork and recognize the conservative ACV in the forecast today.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
